title: Determine Surface Area of Pyramids
objective: I can find the surface area of a pyramid by adding the base area and the lateral faces.
model: net of a pyramid (base polygon plus triangular faces whose height is the slant height)

widgets.where: Practice §4 items 1-6 and Challenge §1 items 1-6 (gen:surfaceAreaPyramid L1-L4)
widgets.component: generated pyramid surface-area problems with a drawn triangle (a lateral face or the base triangle)
widgets.root: viz shape 'tri' stands in for a pyramid. For the square-pyramid variants the figure is one lateral face (base 12, dashed altitude 9), which is correct but cannot show the square base, the four faces, the apex or the difference between the slant height and the pyramid's vertical height; its text label is a bare '9 ft' and its alt text calls the dashed segment 'height', the exact word the lesson separates from 'slant height'. For the triangular-base variants (about 28% of L3 and 34% of L4 draws) the figure is the base triangle (a 9-12-15 right triangle with a dashed leg labelled like a height) while the question is about the three lateral faces with a slant height of 8 ft that is not drawn anywhere. The cube-with-pyramid-on-top variants (35% of L4) are drawn as a single triangle. The aspect is clamped to 0.8-3, so 8-10% of the faces (6 ft base, 15 ft slant) are drawn up to 2 times too wide. Arithmetic and the sweep of dims are consistent.
widgets.replacement: Add the viz kind 'pyramid' to assets/studio-viz-geo.js: {"t":"pyramid","n":4,"base":12,"slant":9,"unit":"ft","labels":true,"vh":null,"net":false}. Oblique view of a square pyramid with the apex above the base centre, hidden base edges dashed, the base edge labelled, and on the front face the slant height drawn dashed from the apex to the midpoint of the base edge with a right-angle mark and the label 'slant height 9 ft'. When a vertical height is given (Challenge 4.2, 5.2) draw it dotted from the apex to the base centre labelled 'height 12 ft (not used for a face)'. With "net":true draw the cross net: one square with a triangle on each side, each triangle labelled base and slant height. For n:3 draw the triangular base with a triangle on each side and the same slant-height marks. In gen:surfaceAreaPyramid replace every viz 'tri' by 'pyramid' (the cube-plus-pyramid variant draws the cube under the pyramid), and change the alt text to say 'slant height'.

widgets.component: Connect check: 'What is the area of one triangular face?', 'What is the total glass area for all four faces?', 'What will the glass cost?' (now carried with the Connect scenario text and the Connect diagram)
widgets.root: The scenario is now shown, but the figure is the Connect bar chart (bars Base (open) 0, Face 1-4 = 6 each with show:true): the bars print 6 for each face and 0 for the open base, which are the answers to items 1 and 2 (6 and 4 × 6). A bar chart is also not a picture of the solid or figure the questions are about. The item is answered by reading the chart.
widgets.replacement: Do not carry a bar-chart diagram into the Mastery section (diagramToViz should return null for kind 'bar-chart', or set show:false until after the answer is checked). Attach instead the pyramid with its slant height marked, using the new "pyramid" viz specified for gen:surfaceAreaPyramid: {"t":"pyramid","n":4,"base":3,"slant":4,"unit":"ft","labels":true}, and show the bars only in the explanation after the student answers.

widgets.component: table comparing a square pyramid (slant height 8) and a rectangular prism (height 8) on the same base: base area 36, lateral area, total
widgets.root: The table prints only 'base area 36' and '36 (× 2 bases)'; the 6 × 6 base appears only in the hint ladder. A base area of 36 does not give the prism's lateral area (a 4 × 9 base has the same area but a different perimeter), so the printed 192 and 264 are underdetermined and the row cannot be completed from what is on screen.
widgets.replacement: Put the base in the row labels and the stem: 'Both solids stand on a 6 in by 6 in square base and are 8 in tall (the pyramid's 8 in is its slant height).' Rename the rows 'Square pyramid, base 6 × 6, slant height 8' and 'Rectangular prism, base 6 × 6, height 8' and keep the keys 96 / 132 and 192 / 264. Attach the new 'pyramid' viz and a prism viz side by side.

widgets.component: the 'Build it, move it, test it' lab: sort measurements by whether the surface area needs them, match beacons to surface areas, tap the slant height from a surface area of 48
widgets.root: The lab has nothing to build or move; the lesson's idea (a pyramid unfolds into a square and triangles whose height is the slant height, not the vertical height) is never manipulated, and the sort is the only place the slant-versus-vertical distinction is tested.
widgets.replacement: Build act kind 'pyrnet' (assets/studio-act/pyrnet.js): a base-edge stepper (2-12) and a slant-height slider show the pyramid and its net side by side with an Unfold button; the readout lists base e × e, one face ½ × e × s, four faces and the total using the student's numbers. A second 'vertical height' slider is a decoy that changes the picture but never the surface area, so the student sees which length belongs in the formula. Tasks: L3 'build a pyramid whose surface area is 144' (e = 6, s = 9 among several valid pairs, rules like 'the slant height is 1.5 times the edge'); L4 triangular-base pyramid with the three slant heights equal. Grade on the measure; feedback names forgot-the-base, forgot-the-½ and used-the-vertical-height.

widgets.root: Recomputed 207, 360, 336, Mira is right (B's faces are bigger), 217, the face height is the slant height 13 m, 9 × 9 + 4 × (½ × 9 × 11), 120 ft² (no base), $432. 4.2 uses a genuine 5-12-13 triangle for the vertical/slant pair.

formulaOrder.formula: SA = base area + 4 × (½ × base edge × slant height)
